what: A perf ablation done by editing kernel sources and then restoring them (cp of the original file) left stale ablated kernel binaries in the JIT cache (built/tt-metal-cache*/kernels/<kernel>). Later runs of the unmodified op silently ran the ablated binaries: NaN outputs with compute-only timings (2.9/6.1 us vs 8.7/130 us), until the op kernel cache dirs were deleted. Unchecked timing harnesses report such runs as valid numbers.
suggest: In the perf guidance (master.md / perf refinement prompt / verifier Gate-on-headroom section): run ablations as define-gated variants via KernelDescriptor.defines (part of the kernel hash), never by editing and restoring sources; if a source edit is unavoidable, delete built/tt-metal-cache*/kernels/<op kernels> afterwards and re-run a correctness-checked case. Also worth root-causing why the dephash check did not invalidate.

what: No documented way to get device kernel time for ad-hoc kernel/plan variants. run_safe_pytest.sh --profile failed (tracy-capture exited 3, no CSV). The working route was undocumented: run a throwaway test dir through eval/eval_test_runner.sh and wrap the op call in eval.metrics_plugin.op_window(). Without the strict window, the whole-body fallback window gave misleading numbers.
suggest: Document a minimal device-timing harness for variant sweeps in the verifier/perf prompts: a test file that wraps the op in metrics_plugin.op_window(), monkeypatches select_plan / KernelDescriptor.defines, checks correctness, and is run with eval_test_runner.sh, reading device_kernel_ns from test_results.json.
